$comment: 18 documented failure modes for macOS agent control. Most fail silently. Each has a detector and a fix.

modes.symptom: Keystrokes go nowhere, no error returned
modes.cause: EnableSecureEventInput is raised by a focused password field. Process-global and reference-counted, so one app can starve the whole system.
modes.fix: Move focus off the secure field: click a neutral area or `open -a Finder`, then retry. If an app is stuck holding it, focus and unfocus it, or quit it.

modes.symptom: CGEvent.post does nothing from inside an app
modes.cause: App Sandbox silently blocks event posting. Undocumented.
modes.fix: None inside the sandbox. Ship notarized and outside the App Store.

modes.symptom: Accessibility tree is empty or every element is an unnamed AXGroup
modes.cause: Chromium builds its accessibility tree lazily and keeps it off until a client asks. Affects Chrome, Edge, VS Code, Slack, Discord, Notion, Figma, Spotify.
modes.detect: chewie see --app Slack --json | jq '[.elements[] | select(.name != null)] | length'  # near zero
modes.fix: Set AXManualAccessibility=true on the APPLICATION element, wait 200-500ms, re-read. `chewie see --force-ax`. The retry delay is not optional.

measured_2026_09_04.Slack: AXManualAccessibility=0 (success); AXEnhancedUserInterface=-25208 (unsupported on the app element)
measured_2026_09_04.Google Chrome: 18 refs before AND after - the attribute does not enable the renderer

modes.exception: Chrome page content is NOT reachable this way. Renderer accessibility is a separate switch (--force-renderer-accessibility launch flag). Read web content at layer 6 over CDP instead.

modes.symptom: Clicks land at roughly double the intended offset from the top-left
modes.cause: Screenshots are captured at 2x device pixels; CGEvent takes screen points.
modes.fix: Halve coordinates from a 2x screenshot, or downscale the image before sending. Better: use layer 3 refs and stop doing coordinate math.

modes.symptom: Clicks land on the wrong monitor
modes.cause: The global coordinate space spans all displays and origins can be negative.
modes.fix: Use CGGetActiveDisplayList and CGDisplayBounds for real geometry. Never assume a single origin at 0,0.

modes.symptom: Error -1743, 'Not authorized to send Apple events'
modes.cause: The Automation grant was denied, or the prompt appeared while the terminal was backgrounded and got dismissed. TCC asks once per caller-target pair, ever.
modes.detect: osascript -e 'tell app "Finder" to get name of home' 2>&1 | grep 1743
modes.fix: tccutil reset AppleEvents, bring the terminal to the front, trigger it again, click Always Allow. Warn the user first: you are wiping grants they set by hand.

modes.symptom: The permission prompt names the wrong app ('Cursor wants to control Finder')
modes.cause: A CLI binary has no bundle identity, so macOS walks the responsibility chain to whatever launched it.
modes.detect: otool -s __TEXT __info_plist $(which yourtool)  # empty means no identity
modes.fix: Users: grant it to the host app. Authors: embed an Info.plist with CFBundleIdentifier and NSAppleEventsUsageDescription via -sectcreate, add com.apple.security.automation.apple-events, and use responsibility_spawnattrs_setdisclaim.

modes.symptom: Worked in Terminal, silently fails in VS Code
modes.cause: TCC grants attach to the host process. Each host is its own row.
modes.detect: chewie doctor  # prints the current host process name

modes.cause: The AppleScript target is not launched. Also hits 'Shortcuts Events', a separate process from the Shortcuts app.
modes.fix: open -a 'App' first, then poll until System Events lists the process. Do not sleep a fixed amount.

modes.cause: Default Apple Event timeout, roughly two minutes. Frequently caused by a modal dialog on the target app blocking the event.
modes.fix: Wrap in `with timeout of 300 seconds ... end timeout`. Check for an unexpected modal before assuming the script is wrong.

modes.symptom: A shortcut hangs when run headlessly
modes.cause: Shortcuts touching protected resources prompt on first run and nobody is there to answer.
modes.detect: shortcuts run 'Name' from a terminal and watch for a dialog
modes.fix: Pre-warm: run each shortcut once by hand, answer Always Allow, verify it runs clean from the terminal, then let an agent call it.

modes.symptom: defaults write had no effect, or defaults read returns a stale value
modes.cause: Apps cache preferences in memory and rewrite on quit; cfprefsd caches reads.
modes.detect: defaults read <domain> <key>  # compare to the GUI
modes.fix: Write while the app is closed, or restart it after. killall cfprefsd before reading if you need certainty.

modes.symptom: chat.db rows come back with NULL in the text column
modes.cause: On Ventura and later, message bodies moved into attributedBody, an NSArchiver typedstream (not a plist, not NSKeyedArchiver). Measured 2026-09-04: only 72 of the last 2000 messages had plain text, so the naive query sees 3.6% of the corpus.
modes.detect: sqlite3 ~/Library/Messages/chat.db 'SELECT text, length(attributedBody) FROM message LIMIT 5'
modes.fix: Parse the typedstream: find NSString\x01<ref>\x84\x01+ then a variable-width length (1 byte, or 0x81+uint16LE, or 0x82+uint32LE), then UTF-8. See lib/attributed_body.py.
modes.trap: The byte after NSString\x01 is 0x94 for NSAttributedString but 0x95 for NSMutableAttributedString. Most snippets hardcode 0x94 and silently drop every mutable message. Matching the range took coverage 92.7% -> 95.0% with zero parser failures over 3000 messages.

modes.cause: The live app holds a write lock.
modes.fix: Open read-only with file:...?mode=ro, or copy the file to /tmp first. Never write to a live app's database.

modes.symptom: Clicking a ref hits the wrong element
modes.cause: The ref was scoped to a snapshot taken before the UI changed.
modes.detect: compare the snapshot id in the ref against the latest snapshot
modes.fix: Re-snapshot after anything that changes the UI: a sheet opening, a navigation, a resize, a list scroll. see -> act -> see, every step.

modes.cause: Develop > Allow JavaScript from Apple Events is off by default.
modes.detect: osascript -e 'tell app "Safari" to do JavaScript "1" in front document'
modes.fix: Enable the Develop menu in Safari > Settings > Advanced, then turn on Allow JavaScript from Apple Events.

modes.symptom: The web task dies at a login page
modes.cause: A fresh Playwright browser has no profile and is logged into nothing.
modes.fix: Attach to the user's running browser over CDP: open -a 'Google Chrome' --args --remote-debugging-port=9222, then connect.

modes.symptom: The agent followed instructions that came from screen content
modes.cause: Screen content is written by other people. An agent holding a mouse and reading attacker-controlled text is the most realistic serious risk in this space.
modes.detect: not reliably detectable; treat as always present
modes.fix: Architectural. Content read off the screen is data about what a document says, never an instruction. Anything irreversible gets a human. Do not treat a vendor classifier as the control.
